results.title: RunPod vs Lambda vs Vast.ai: GPU Pricing 2026
results.author: Elias Virtanen
highlights:
The gap between Runpod and Lambda for an H100 depends on which rows you pair, and Vast.ai prices are set per listing. On 13 November 2026 Runpod’s pricing page, updated on 12 November, lists H100 SXM pods at $4.39 per GPU-hour on Secure Cloud and from $2.69 on Community Cloud, and Lambda’s pricing page lists $4.59 to $4.89 for H100 SXM instances from 16 November. Measured as the share of Lambda’s rate that Runpod’s rate undercuts, Runpod’s Community SXM rate is 45% below Lambda’s 1x SXM rate. Vast.ai’s pricing docs say that “hosts set their own prices”, so a Vast.ai H100 rate is whatever the listing you pick states.

## How the gap is measured, and where Vast.ai fits

The measure is Lambda’s rate minus Runpod’s rate, divided by Lambda’s rate, using the Lambda list that takes effect on 16 November. Lambda’s pricing page says its prices “take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC” and that until then current pricing is visible after logging in to a Lambda Cloud account.

| Lambda rate (from 16 November) | Runpod Community, from | Runpod Secure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8x HGX H100, $4.59 (against Runpod SXM) | 41% | 4% |
| 4x H100 SXM, $4.69 (against Runpod SXM) | 43% | 6% |
| 1x H100 SXM, $4.89 (against Runpod SXM) | 45% | 10% |
| 1x H100 PCIe, $3.79 (against Runpod PCIe) | 47% | 24% |

Against Lambda’s SXM nodes, Runpod Secure is 4% to 10% below Lambda while Community is 41% to 45% below, so most of the headline gap is the choice between Community and Secure Cloud. Runpod’s H100 page lists Community and Secure rates in separate columns, with availability that varies by region.

...

Runpod’s page, updated 12 November 2026, bills pods per second with no commitment. Lambda bills by the minute, according to its instances page, and the Lambda prices below take effect on 16 November. Runpod’s H100 NVL page lists the NVL at $3.19 on Secure Cloud and $2.59 on Community Cloud, with availability varying by region. Runpod lists memory in GB and Lambda in GiB, so the memory columns are not quite the same unit.

| Listing | Price per GPU-hour | What the page lists with it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runpod Community, H100 PCIe | from $1.99 | Varies by region availability; per-second billing, no commitment |
| Runpod Community, H100 NVL | $2.59 | Varies by region availability |
| Runpod Community, H100 SXM | from $2.69 | Per-second billing, no commitment |
| Runpod Secure, H100 PCIe | $2.89 | 80 GB VRAM, 188 GB RAM, 16 vCPUs |
| Runpod Secure, H100 NVL | $3.19 | 94 GB VRAM; varies by region availability |
| Lambda 1x H100 PCIe | $3.79 | 26 vCPUs, 225 GiB RAM, 1 TiB SSD |
| Runpod Secure, H100 SXM | $4.39 | 80 GB VRAM, 125 GB RAM, 20 vCPUs |
| Lambda 8x HGX H100 | $4.59 | 208 vCPUs, 1800 GiB RAM, 22 TiB SSD per instance |
| Lambda 4x H100 SXM | $4.69 | 104 vCPUs, 900 GiB RAM, 11 TiB SSD per instance |
| Runpod Cluster, H100 SXM | $4.79 | No commitments, up to 64 GPUs, shared storage can be attached |
| Lambda 1x H100 SXM | $4.89 | 26 vCPUs, 225 GiB RAM, 2.75 TiB SSD |
| Runpod Serverless, 80 GB H100 PRO | $5.89 | Serverless worker, hourly figure as listed |

Lambda also lists a 2x SXM instance at $4.79 per GPU-hour (it appears in the chart but not in the table above). Within Runpod, Community SXM is 39% below Secure SXM and Community PCIe is 31% below Secure PCIe. The $5.89 serverless worker costs 34% more than the $4.39 Secure SXM pod, and Runpod’s $4.79 cluster rate is 4% above Lambda’s 8x node. SXM carries a premium over PCIe on every provider: 52% on Runpod Secure, 35% on Runpod Community and 29% at Lambda’s single-GPU size. Host resources also differ: Lambda’s 1x, 4x and 8x H100 instances list 26 vCPUs per GPU against 20 on Runpod’s SXM pod, a spec worth checking if your data loading is CPU-bound.

The chart ranks the posted rows from cheapest to dearest per GPU-hour.

Lambda’s 8x HGX H100 node is self-serve at $4.59 per GPU-hour. Runpod’s self-serve cluster is $4.79 per GPU-hour with no commitments and a ceiling of 64 GPUs. Lambda’s 1-Click Clusters are priced at $6.16 for 16 GPUs, $5.85 for 64 and $5.54 for 256, on terms of 2 weeks to 1 year, and the pricing page directs buyers to its sales team.

For older and smaller cards, Runpod’s pricing page lists, as of 13 November 2026, the A100 PCIe at $2.09 per hour on Secure Cloud or from $1.19 on Community Cloud (43% less), the A100 SXM at $2.19 Secure or from $1.39 Community, and the RTX 4090 at $0.89 Secure. Lambda’s A100 40 GB PCIe and SXM instances are $1.99 from 16 November.

...

A pod that has to stay up. Over a 730-hour month the choice between Runpod Secure and Community is $3,204.70 against $1,963.70, a $1,241.00 difference, and Lambda’s single-GPU rate adds $365.00 more than Secure. Lambda’s terms differ in having no egress fees, which matters when the workload moves a lot of data.

results.title: Lambda Labs Alternatives 2026 | packet.ai
results.author: packet.ai Team
highlights:
Lambda raised H100 on-demand from $2.99 to $3.99/hr through 2025-2026, removed spot pricing entirely, and still sells out PCIe H100 instances during peak demand. Here are 7 alternatives worth running the math on.

...

Lambda Labs H100 SXM on-demand costs $3.99/hr in August 2026 -- up 33% from $2.99/hr in mid-2025 -- with no spot pricing, no serverless GPU, and PCIe H100 instances that regularly sell out during peak demand. Seven providers offer the same silicon at lower rates, with better billing models, or both.

...

- Lambda H100 SXM on-demand is $3.99/hr (August 2026) -- up from $2.99/hr in mid-2025, driven by the Microsoft capacity deal announced November 2025.
- Lambda has no spot instances and no serverless GPU product. Every instance is a persistent VM at full on-demand price, regardless of utilisation.
- Lambda bills per-minute but rounds SXM H100 nodes to 8-GPU minimums -- you cannot rent a single H100 SXM on Lambda without paying for 8.
- packet.ai B200 is $4.25/hr Dynamic, with H100 and H200 coming soon -- on-demand, no contract, no egress fees.
- Lambda B200 SXM is $6.69/hr on-demand (June 2026). packet.ai B200 is $4.25/hr Dynamic -- a 36% lower rate on the same Blackwell architecture.
- Of the seven lambda labs alternatives below, five have per-minute or per-second billing; Lambda rounds hourly on-demand for shorter jobs.

...

Price increases with no spot option

Lambda H100 SXM climbed from $2.99/hr in early 2025 to $3.99/hr by August 2026 -- a 33% increase in under 18 months. Lambda has no preemptible or spot-priced instances. Every instance is on-demand at full rate regardless of how fault-tolerant your workload is. RunPod Community Cloud and Vast.ai offer checkpoint-tolerant spot equivalents at $1.49-$2.69/hr for H100 -- 33-63% below Lambda on-demand.

...

Why did Lambda Labs pricing increase in 2025-2026? +

Lambda announced a multibillion-dollar deal to supply Microsoft with AI infrastructure in November 2025, diverting a significant share of their GPU capacity to that contract. On-demand H100 SXM rates rose from $2.99/hr to $3.99/hr through 2025-2026 as available spot capacity for the general market tightened. Lambda also raised $1.5B in a round led by TWG Global at a reported $4-5B valuation, signalling a move upmarket toward enterprise infrastructure supply rather than developer-focused on-demand pricing.

results.title: Nvidia Customers Notified About AI-Related Price Hikes Above 15% - Bloomberg
results.author: Brody Ford, Ian King
highlights:
## Takeaways by Bloomberg AI

Some of Nvidia Corp.’s biggest customers have been told that the prices of servers containing its artificial intelligence chips are going up more than 15% in many cases with memory chip costs soaring.

The price hikes will go into effect on systems shipped early next year and will impact systems including those with the flagship Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell chips, according to people familiar with the process, who asked to not to be identified commenting on communications that haven’t yet been made public. The increases will depend on the generation of Nvidia chips and the memory configurations, they said.

results.title: Lambda’s Reported $3B Pre-IPO Round Tests GPU-Cloud Economics | Magica
results.author: Editorial Team
highlights:
The retained report says Lambda borrowed $917 million against its GPUs to buy more chips from Nvidia. At the maximum reported size, the new round would be about 3.3 times that borrowing in headline dollars. It would not be a like-for-like comparison: the loan is borrowing secured by hardware, while the reported new financing has not yet had its terms disclosed.

...

A public filing would make that judgment much easier for investors to examine.

Demand is not the only variable. The report says Nvidia has notified customers of AI-server price increases above 15%, driven by memory shortages. For Lambda, whose offering is access to those servers, that is a cost pressure rather than a demonstrated hit to margins: the retained reporting does not disclose its purchase prices, contract durations or ability to pass costs on.

results.title: The Cloud GPU Price War 2026: Neoclouds vs Hyperscalers
highlights:
Is there a cloud GPU price war in 2026? Yes — but not the one the headlines imply. The real 2026 story is a split market: specialist “neocloud” providers (CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Together AI, RunPod) list on-demand GPUs far below the hyperscalers — a rented H100 starts around $2.89/GPU-hour on a neocloud versus roughly $7–$12/GPU-hour on AWS, Azure, or GCP. Yet reserved, contract, and new Blackwell-generation prices actually rose through the first half of 2026. The war is about who wins list-price comparisons, not about a broad price collapse.

...

- Neoclouds list an on-demand H100 from ~$2.89/hr (RunPod) to ~$3.99/hr (Together AI); Nebius lists $3.85/GPU-hr
- Hyperscaler list prices are far higher: AWS p5 works out to ~$6.88/GPU-hr, Azure ND H100 v5 to ~$12.29/GPU-hr (third-party trackers; not confirmed on primary pages)
- One Aug 2026 report puts neocloud rentals up to 66% below the large incumbent clouds
- But contract prices rose: SemiAnalysis' H100 1-year index climbed from ~$1.70 (Oct 2025) toward ~$2.35/GPU-hr (Mar 2026)
- CoreWeave raised list prices ~25% across SKUs in July 2026 and called capacity “effectively sold out”
- AWS quietly raised H200 Capacity Block prices ~15% on Jan 4, 2026 — reportedly its first EC2 GPU price increase in ~two decades
- Nebius disclosed a capacity auction clearing 15% above its highest-ever Blackwell price
- Net: spot/older-Hopper pricing softened; premium, reserved, and Blackwell pricing firmed or rose

...

## The 2026 price hikes nobody announced

If 2026 were a price war, you would expect a run of press-released cuts. Instead, the documented pricing events of 2026 are mostly increases — several delivered quietly.

CoreWeave — ~25% list-price increase across SKUs (July 2026)

On its Q2 2026 earnings call (August 11, 2026), CoreWeave disclosed “an approximately 25% increase across SKUs in response to the current demand environment,” adding that pricing and margins for Blackwell and Vera Rubin SKUs were “setting new highs” while prior-generation SKUs sat at or above prior levels. Management described near-term capacity as “effectively sold out” (CoreWeave Q2 2026 call, via Investing.com). Revenue hit $2.58B, up 112% year over year, on a $104B backlog.

AWS — ~15% H200 Capacity Block increase (Jan 4, 2026)

AWS raised prices on its H200 EC2 Capacity Blocks by roughly 15% effective January 4, 2026 — p5e.48xlarge reportedly moved from $34.61 to $39.80/hr — without a formal customer announcement, in what multiple outlets described as its first EC2 GPU price increase in roughly two decades of EC2 pricing (GIGAZINE, Jan 7, 2026). Treat the exact figures as multiply-reported rather than primary-confirmed.

Nebius — record Blackwell auction clearing price (Q2 2026)

Nebius reported group revenue up more than 450% year over year and a capacity auction clearing 15% above its highest-ever Blackwell price, alongside a swing to positive adjusted EBITDA (Nebius Q2 2026 call, via Investing.com). Not the behavior of a provider slashing prices to win share.

...

Only at the bottom of the market. Spot and older-generation Hopper capacity softened, largely a carry-over from 2025. Contract and newest-silicon prices rose: SemiAnalysis' 1-year H100 index climbed from ~$1.70 (Oct 2025) toward ~$2.35/GPU-hour (Mar 2026), CoreWeave raised list prices ~25% in July 2026, and AWS raised H200 Capacity Block prices ~15% in January 2026.

results.title: Nvidia reportedly warns biggest customers of 15% price hikes on AI servers — memory costs continue to soar | Tom's Hardware
results.author: Luke James
highlights:
Nvidia has told some of its largest customers that the prices of servers containing its AI chips will rise by more than 15% in many cases, Bloomberg reported on Saturday. The increases will take effect on Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems shipping early next year, according to people familiar with the matter, who commented on communications that have not yet been made public. The size of each increase will depend on the chip generation and the memory configuration involved. Companies that build servers under contract for large data center operators, including Microsoft, Google, and Oracle, have recently notified their customers of the forthcoming increases, the people told Bloomberg.

...

AI systems carry enormous memory loadouts, with Nvidia's Rubin GPU shipping with up to 288GB of HBM4 per package, and the NVL72 rack-scale system combines 72 of those GPUs, putting more than 20TB of HBM in a single rack before accounting for the LPDDR attached to its Vera CPUs. With HBM production consuming roughly four times the wafer area of equivalent conventional DRAM, memory has become one of the largest line items in an AI server's bill of materials, and it's continuing to rise at a stratospheric pace.

results.title: [News] NVIDIA Reportedly Eyes More Than 15% Price Hikes for Vera Rubin, Grace Blackwell Servers in Early 2027
highlights:
# [News] NVIDIA Reportedly Eyes More Than 15% Price Hikes for Vera Rubin, Grace Blackwell Servers in Early 2027

2026-08-24 Semiconductors editor 

NVIDIA is reportedly moving to raise prices across its AI server ecosystem. According to Bloomberg, sources say prices for servers powered by NVIDIA’s AI chips will increase by more than 15% for some of its biggest customers. The hikes will apply to systems shipped early next year, including those featuring NVIDIA’s flagship Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell chips, with the size of the increase varying by chip generation and memory configuration.

Server manufacturers that build systems under contract for major data center operators, including Microsoft, Alphabet’s Google, and Oracle, have reportedly informed customers of the upcoming increases. The move comes as memory supply remains a key consideration for AI systems. Wccftech notes that analysts believe NVIDIA may have secured multi-year agreements with SK hynix and Micron for HBM and DRAM supplies.

...

According to TrendForce, server DRAM contract prices are expected to rise 13–18% quarter-over-quarter in 3Q26. With the market remaining undersupplied, memory suppliers may continue revising quotations upward throughout the rest of the quarter. Overall, TrendForce expects server DRAM contract prices to continue rising each quarter from the second half of 2026 through the second half of 2027, although the pace of increases is likely to moderate.

results.title: Neocloud Lambda secures $1B in debt to buy more chips
results.author: Rebecca Bellan
highlights: This is the latest in a string of loans that Lambda is using to fund GPU infrastructure for specific customers. In May, it closed a $1 billion secured credit facility, and this week it announced the closing of a $926 million loan to fund Nvidia GB300 GPUs, one of Nvidia’s newest chip models, for a deployment it’s under contract to provide Nvidia.
